transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you. Well, honestly, I'm just... I'm at my wit's end, I really am. I’m here because work has just become this dark cloud over my entire life. I’ve been a quality inspector for years—I check, sort, sample, I know my job inside and out, and I've never had a problem. But we got this new operations manager recently, and ever since he started, he's just been constantly picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. Procedures that work perfectly fine, mind you! 

And it's gotten to the point where I just... I can’t seem to leave work at work anymore. I used to be able to just clock out and be done, but now I come home completely wound up. My poor husband, I just snap at him over the tiniest little things, like if he left a dish in the sink, which isn't like me at all and isn't fair to him. And then at night, I just lie awake for hours in the dark, tossing and turning, replaying every single meeting and every little comment this manager made during the day. It's exhausting. And because of all that, the next day I go in and I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls on the line—calls I used to make without even a second thought, without any trouble at all. I'm hesitating over things I've done a thousand times. I just feel like I'm losing my grip on everything because of this guy, and I don't know how to turn it off.
Do you find yourself worrying or feeling anxious about things other than work when you're lying awake at night?

No, honestly, that's the strange part about all of this. If you had asked me a year ago... I mean, my life outside of that building is actually very quiet. Very settled. My husband and I, we've been in our house for twenty years, the mortgage is manageable, we don't have any big family drama going on. I mean, sure, there's the normal everyday things, like hoping the car doesn't need new brakes this winter or whatever, but absolutely nothing that keeps me up. 

No, when I'm lying there staring at the ceiling fan at 2 AM, it is one hundred percent just... him. The manager. And the line. I don't worry about my health or my marriage—well, other than feeling guilty for snapping at my husband, like I mentioned—but the actual anxiety, the spinning thoughts? It's just work, work, work. I just keep seeing the sorting bins in my head, and I hear his voice asking me why I pulled a certain batch for testing when the variance was within his new, ridiculous parameters. Parameters that make no practical sense on the floor, by the way! It's like my brain is a broken record, and it's only got this one awful song to play, and I can't skip the track to think about anything else, not even if I try. I'll lay there and try to force myself to think about the garden, or what I'm going to plant this spring, and boom, within thirty seconds I'm right back on the factory floor, arguing with him in my head about the sampling weights. So, no, it's really just the job. That's what's so frustrating, it's taking over everything else.
Have you been avoiding certain tasks or situations at work since the new operations manager started?

Well, yes, actually. I have been. I mean, it’s really embarrassing to admit because I’ve always prided myself on my work ethic—twenty years without a single write-up—but my work record has really taken a hit lately. I’ve actually been missing internal deadlines, which is just so completely unlike me. Usually, I have my inspection logs submitted to the floor supervisor by 3 PM sharp, but lately, I’m just... I’m avoiding finalizing them because I know the new manager might review them. So I second-guess my numbers, I sit on the paperwork, and then suddenly the deadline is blown. 

And the meetings! Oh, the meetings. We have these weekly cross-departmental huddles that I am absolutely expected to attend as the senior inspector, but I’ve just been pulling back from them completely. I’ll make up an excuse, I'll say I have a critical batch of parts to sort, or I'll just hide out in the testing lab, just so I don't have to sit in the same room as him and wait for him to undermine my procedures in front of everybody. It’s terrible, I know it makes me look bad to the rest of the team, but I just can't face it right now. I just want to avoid him at all costs.

And the worst part is, it’s not just the job, it’s spilling over into everything else. Like I was saying before about snapping at my husband... we are just arguing so much more lately. We usually have this really nice evening routine, you know? We'd cook dinner together, maybe watch a little TV, just unwind and talk about our days. But I’m just not keeping up with any of that the way I used to. I come through the door, I drop my bag, and I just... I don't want to cook, I don't want to chat, I just want to sit on the couch and be left alone. And then he gets frustrated because I'm not engaging, or I bite his head off over something silly, and then we're bickering... It's just a mess. I feel like I'm letting everything slide, at the plant and in my own house, all because I'm just trying to dodge this one guy and the stress he brings.
Have you been feeling hopeless or depressed most of the time since the new operations manager started?

Hopeless? No, no, I wouldn't use that word at all. I mean, honestly, if I'm being completely truthful, the only thing I'm hoping for is that he gets transferred to another plant! But no, I don't feel depressed in that way. Like, I'm not walking around feeling sorry for myself or feeling like there's no point to anything in life. It's not a sadness, if that makes sense? It's more of an intense... aggravation. A constant buzzing in my head. 

I still care about things. I still want to have those nice evenings with my husband, I still want to do my job well—that's the whole reason I'm so upset, because I care so much about the quality of the parts going out the door. If I were depressed, I think I'd just stop caring altogether, right? I'd just let him ruin the inspection protocols and pass bad batches and not even bat an eye. But I do care. I care deeply. I've spent twenty years building my reputation on that floor, making sure every sample is weighed and sorted to the exact millimeter of the spec, and I'm just fighting to protect that. 

So it's not hopelessness. It's just that I'm so consumed by the injustice of it all, and the sheer stress of dealing with his micromanaging, that I just don't have the bandwidth for my normal life right now. I'm exhausted, and I'm angry, and I'm constantly on edge waiting for his next ridiculous email, but I definitely wouldn't say I'm sitting around feeling depressed. I just want things to go back to the way they were before he walked through those doors, because everything was perfectly fine, my life was perfectly fine, before him.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, or trembling when you're at work or thinking about work?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not breaking out in a cold sweat or shaking like a leaf or anything dramatic like that. I know some people get panic attacks where their heart just races out of their chest, my sister actually gets those sometimes, but that's not me. 

Now, I will say, when I see him walking down the aisle toward my station—he has this very distinct walk, very heavy on his heels, you can hear him coming over the hum of the machinery—I definitely feel my stomach just... drop. It's like a knot tightens right right below my ribs, and my jaw clenches up. I actually caught myself grinding my teeth the other day while I was trying to recalibrate the digital scale after he had messed with the settings. But it's not like my heart is fluttering or I'm dizzy or anything. It's more of a whole-body tension. Like I'm bracing for impact, you know? 

Even when I'm driving to work, pulling into the parking lot and seeing his ridiculous oversized truck taking up two spaces near the entrance, I just feel my shoulders hike up to my ears. I probably carry a lot of the stress in my neck and back, honestly. But as far as palpitations or sweating or trembling? No, nothing like that. Just that awful, tight feeling of knowing I'm going to have to spend the next eight hours defending every single measurement I take.
Do you find yourself having repetitive, intrusive thoughts about your work or the new operations manager outside of work or when you're trying to fall asleep?

Oh my goodness, yes. That is exactly it. It's like a broken record in my head that I just can't unplug. Honestly, that’s the main reason I’m here talking to you, because ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years—procedures that have always worked perfectly fine, mind you—I just cannot seem to leave work at work anymore. 

It used to be that I'd punch out, get in my car, and the plant was out of my mind until the next morning. But now? I come home completely wound up, like a coiled spring. I walk through the door and I'm still arguing with him in my head, which is why I end up snapping at my husband the second he asks me a simple question about dinner. And nighttime is the absolute worst. I’ll get into bed, try to settle down, and the minute I close my eyes, I am just lying awake replaying every single meeting from that day. I'll obsess over a comment he made about my sampling methods, or I'll play out entirely new arguments, thinking of all the things I *should* have said when he questioned my documentation in front of the junior techs. 

It just loops and loops. I'll watch the clock turn to 1 AM, then 2 AM, and I'm just stewing in it. And then, because I've spent half the night obsessing over this guy, I go into work the next day exhausted and completely in my own head. It’s gotten to the point where I actually find myself second-guessing routine quality calls that I used to make without any trouble at all. Things I've done a thousand times! I'll be looking at a part, knowing it passes spec, but my hand will hover over the sorting bin because I'm terrified he's going to pull the batch and re-measure it just to try and prove me wrong. It’s this horrible cycle—I stress all day, I bring it home, I stay awake analyzing it, and then I doubt myself the next day. I just can't shut my brain off.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships or daily activities because of your preoccupation with work and the new operations manager?

Well, yes, absolutely. I mean, it's bleeding into everything, and that's what's so frustrating because I've always prided myself on being someone who can handle her business, you know? But at work, my record has definitely taken a hit. I’ve actually missed a couple of internal deadlines for submitting my weekly quality reports, which is completely unlike me. I used to have those on my supervisor's desk by 3 PM every Friday, like clockwork, for twenty years. But now, because I'm double and triple-checking every single measurement out of fear that this guy is going to ambush me, it takes me twice as long to do half the work. And I've started pulling back from the morning production meetings, too. I'm supposed to be there to give the QA perspective, but I just... I can't stomach sitting in that conference room listening to him talk about "efficiency metrics" when he doesn't even understand how the digital scales operate. So I'll find excuses to skip them, or I'll just stay at my station and say I'm backed up on sampling, which, to be fair, I usually am lately.

And then at home... poor Mark. My husband, Mark. We are definitely arguing more. A lot more. And it's not even about big things, it's just that my fuse is so incredibly short right now. He'll ask me if I want to watch our usual Tuesday night show, or if we should start getting dinner ready, and I'll just snap at him. I'm not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to, at all. We used to cook together, go for a walk around the neighborhood if the weather was nice, just talk about our days. But now? I come home, drop my bag, and I just kind of collapse into the recliner. I don't want to cook, I don't want to walk, I don't even really want to talk, because if I open my mouth, all that comes out is complaining about work. And I know it's not fair to him. I know he's getting the absolute worst version of me right now, but I just don't have the energy left for our life after spending eight hours fighting for my professional dignity, you know? It's just... it's taking a toll on everything.
Have you been avoiding talking to your coworkers or participating in social interactions at work because of the new operations manager?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding people entirely, but... it's definitely different now. I mean, I've worked there for twenty years, right? I know everyone on the floor. I know their kids' names, I know who's retiring next year, I know who brings the good donuts on Fridays. We used to have this really great dynamic, especially around the breakroom. You know, you'd go in to grab a coffee, and you'd end up chatting for ten minutes about the weekend or whatever. It was nice. It made the day go by faster.

But lately? I just... I don't know, I don't really have it in me. It's not that I'm hiding from my coworkers, exactly. It's more that I just don't want to talk about him, and that's all anyone seems to be talking about. Or, worse, I'm afraid that if I do start talking, I won't be able to stop, and I'll just sound like a crazy person complaining about the same things over and over again. I mean, I know I'm already doing that at home with Mark, and I don't want to be "that" person at work, you know? The bitter older woman who can't handle change. That's not who I am. 

So, I guess I have been keeping to myself a bit more. Like, instead of eating my lunch in the breakroom where he might walk in—because he does that now, he just strolls in during our lunch hour to "check in," which really means he's checking to see who's taking too long—I've been going out to my car. I'll just sit in the parking lot, listen to the radio, and eat my sandwich alone. It's quiet. It's the only time during the day where I feel like I don't have to be on guard. And if someone comes up to my station to chat, I keep it really brief. I just focus on the parts in front of me, give a quick smile, and get back to work. I just don't have the bandwidth for the office politics right now, not when I'm already spending so much mental energy just trying to do my job without getting a lecture on efficiency. So, yeah, I guess I am pulling back socially, but it's not because I don't like my coworkers. It's just... survival mode, I suppose.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges to perform specific rituals or behaviors outside of work that are not related to your job or the new operations manager?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't have any strange habits or urges to do things over and over, if that's what you mean. I've always been a fairly organized person, of course. I think you kind of have to be when you do quality assurance for a living—you get used to things being orderly and following a specific standard, so it naturally kind of spills over into how you keep your house. 

So, sure, I like my kitchen counters wiped down a certain way, and I have a specific system for how I load the dishwasher... Mark always tries to put the cereal bowls on the bottom rack, and I just have to sigh and move them to the top because they just don't get the right water pressure down there, you know? But that’s just... that's just normal household stuff, just liking things done right. It's not some uncontrollable urge or a ritual I have to do or else I'll panic. I'm not checking the front door locks ten times before bed or washing my hands until they're raw or anything like you hear about. 

Honestly, doctor, I don't even think I would have the brain capacity to obsess over anything else right now even if I wanted to. Every single spare thought, every ounce of mental energy I have is just completely eaten up by that new manager and the absolute mess he's making of my department. It’s like he’s taking up all the room in my head, so there's no space left for anything else, let alone some new ritual or habit. So, no, outside of all the stress with the plant and my job, I don't have anything like that going on. I’m just... well, I’m just trying to get by. When I actually have the energy to do my normal routines, which really isn't very often these days anyway, I just do them normally.
Have you felt like your ability to function at work or at home has been significantly impacted by your thoughts and feelings about the new operations manager?

Well, yes, absolutely. I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record here, and like I was telling you just a few minutes ago, it really has just upended my entire life. My ability to function is just... it's just shot, doctor. 

At work, my record has taken a massive hit, which just kills me. I mean, I’ve missed those internal deadlines I was talking about, and for someone who has been there twenty years with a spotless file, that is a huge deal. It's embarrassing, honestly. And I’ve pulled back from the morning production meetings that I’m absolutely expected to attend. I'm supposed to be the voice of quality assurance in those rooms, but I just can't do it right now, I can't function in there with him running the show. 

And then, you know, I pack up all that stress and I drag it right through my front door. Like I said about Mark, we are just arguing so much more lately. It breaks my heart because he doesn't deserve it, but I'm just not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to. The cooking together, the walks, just being a normal married couple... all of that is just gone. I just come home and shut down. So, yes, to answer your question, my functioning is definitely impacted. I feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water anywhere I go.
Do you feel like your relationships with friends and family outside of your husband are also being affected by your stress and anxiety about work?

Well, yes, it really does bleed into everything else. I know I'm repeating myself a bit from what I just said a moment ago, but it’s all connected, isn't it? Because my work record is taking such a hit from those missed internal deadlines, and because I’ve been pulling back from those morning meetings I’m expected to attend... it just drains every single ounce of energy I have. 

By the time I get through the day, carrying all that guilt and frustration, there's just nothing left in the tank for anyone. I mean, if I'm already arguing more with my own husband and completely dropping the ball on our usual evening routines, you can imagine I don't have the capacity for anyone else. My sister, for example, she called me three times last week. We usually talk every Sunday afternoon, like clockwork. We’ve done that for years. But lately? I just look at the phone ringing on the kitchen counter and I can't even bring myself to pick it up. 

What am I going to say to her? I'm just going to end up complaining about the plant again, or I'm going to have to pretend everything is fine when it's absolutely not. My best friend from high school, Linda, she wanted to get lunch this past Saturday, and I actually made up an excuse about having a migraine. It feels terrible lying to her like that, but if I go, she's going to ask how I am, and I just don't want to bring everybody down. It’s like, because I’m failing at work, and because Mark and I aren't doing our normal things like cooking together or taking our walks, I just feel like I'm failing across the board. So I just isolate. I don't call anyone back. I just sit in the house, worrying about my job, snapping at Mark, and feeling guilty about ignoring my friends. It’s just exhausting, doctor. It really is.
Do you feel like your problems with the new operations manager are affecting your overall well-being or ability to enjoy things you used to?

Well, yes. Completely. It's just... it's like a dark cloud over everything, really. I know I keep harping on the exact same things today, but it’s because it’s just so overwhelming and I can't seem to escape it. My overall well-being is just in the gutter right now. 

I used to actually enjoy my job, you know? I know quality assurance isn't exactly glamorous to most people, but I liked it. I liked making sure things were done right and keeping our standards high. Now? Like I mentioned before, my work record has taken such a terrible hit, and it just breaks my heart. Missing those internal deadlines—which I never, ever used to do in twenty years—and having to pull back and hide from those morning production meetings I’m absolutely expected to attend... it just eats away at my self-esteem. How can I enjoy anything when I know I'm failing at my job because this new manager is making it impossible to do things the right way? 

And then, it completely ruins my ability to enjoy my home life, too. Like I was saying about Mark... we used to have such nice, quiet evenings. We’d cook dinner together, we’d go for our walks around the neighborhood just to decompress and talk about our days. I really, really looked forward to that part of the day, it was my safe haven. But now, I’m just not keeping up with those usual evening routines at all. The joy is just gone from it. Instead, we’re just arguing more and more. I walk in the door so wound up about the plant, I snap at him over nothing, and then I feel incredibly guilty, and then the whole evening is just ruined. 

So, no, I'm not enjoying much of anything lately. It’s like this whole situation has just robbed me of the things that used to bring me peace, both at work and at home. I just can't seem to shake it off, no matter how hard I try to just leave it at the time clock. It just follows me everywhere.
Are you finding it difficult to engage in or enjoy activities outside of work due to your stress and anxiety about the new operations manager?

Well, yes, I really am finding it difficult, and I know I'm probably starting to sound like a broken record here, just circling back to the same things I was telling you earlier, but it really is all connected. Because of the situation with him, everything outside of work has just lost its color. It's like I have this heavy weight on my chest from the moment I wake up until the moment I go to sleep, and it just crushes any desire to do the things I used to love. 

I mean, like I said before, my work record has taken such a terrible hit. Missing those internal deadlines and pulling back from those morning meetings I'm expected to attend... it's just so unlike me, and it consumes my thoughts even when I'm miles away from the plant. I'll be sitting on my couch on a Saturday, and suddenly I'm agonizing over what might be going wrong on the floor because I wasn't in that meeting to catch it. 

And because my mind is always there, always spinning, it completely ruins my time at home. Like I was saying about Mark, we are arguing so much more lately. We used to have such a nice rhythm, you know? But now I'm just not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to. I don't want to cook, I don't want to go for our walks, I don't even want to sit and watch our favorite shows. I just sit there, stewing about the operations manager and how he's ruining everything I've built over twenty years. So, yes, it's incredibly difficult to engage in anything else. It's like my whole life has just shrunk down to this one awful, stressful situation at the plant, and there's no room left for anything or anyone else, not even the things that used to make me happy.
Are you experiencing any changes in your appetite or sleep pattern since the new operations manager started?

Well, my appetite is about the same, I suppose, I haven't really been paying much attention to food. But my sleep? My sleep is just completely ruined. It’s like... well, I go to bed, right? And I’m already so incredibly wound up from the day. Like I was saying before, I come home carrying all this tension, I end up snapping at Mark over something silly, and then by the time we actually turn the lights out, my brain just absolutely refuses to shut off. 

I just lie awake, staring at the ceiling for hours, replaying all those meetings in my head. Because ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures—procedures I have used for years, by the way, with absolutely no issues from anyone else—I just can’t seem to leave work at work anymore. It follows me right into bed. I play his comments over and over, agonizing over every little detail and wondering what I could have said differently, or what he's going to find fault with tomorrow. 

And then the worst part is what happens the next day. Because I've been up half the night stressing, I go in so tired and so deep in my own head that I actually start second-guessing routine quality calls. Things I used to make without a second thought, without any trouble at all! I mean, I’ve been doing this for twenty years, I know my job, I know what passes and what doesn't. But now? Now I stand there over a sample and just freeze, wondering if he's going to come down to the floor and tear my report apart. It's just a vicious cycle. So, yes, the sleep is just... it's awful, doctor. I can't seem to get a single moment of peace.
Are you feeling like your ability to function and enjoy life is significantly impaired because of your stress and anxiety about the new operations manager?

Well, yes, significantly impaired is exactly how I would describe it. It's just... it's completely taken over my life, to be honest. I know I've said this already, and I really don't mean to just keep repeating myself, but it's hard not to when it's just so all-consuming. It's like I was telling you before about my work record taking such a terrible hit. That's the part that really stings, you know? Because I've always prided myself on being reliable. But now, because I'm so stressed and anxious about every little thing this new manager might do or say, I've actually missed internal deadlines. Me! Missing deadlines! And I've been pulling back and hiding from those morning production meetings that I am absolutely expected to attend. I just can't face him, I can't face the scrutiny, so I just avoid it, and it's ruining my reputation there. 

And then, of course, I carry all of that home with me, like a physical weight, and it just bleeds into everything else. Like I mentioned about Mark... we are just arguing so much more now. It's not even about big things, it's just stupid, little things because my nerves are completely shot by the time I walk through the front door. I'm irritable, I'm exhausted from not sleeping, and I'm just not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to. The dinners, the walks, just sitting down and talking... I don't have the energy or the bandwidth for any of it anymore. My mind is just trapped back at the plant, worrying about what disaster is waiting for me tomorrow. So, yes, my ability to function normally, let alone actually enjoy my life, is just... it's practically non-existent right now because of all this stress. It's just too much.
Are you experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems due to your stress and anxiety about the new operations manager?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I don't get headaches... maybe a slight twinge here and there, but nothing I'd call a real headache, you know? And my stomach... well, like I said before, I haven't really been paying much attention to food, but it's not like I'm having cramps or feeling sick to my stomach or anything like that. It's more just this... this constant, heavy feeling of dread. 

It's funny you ask about physical things, though, because even without the headaches or stomach issues, I just feel physically drained. It's like my whole body is just vibrating with this nervous energy all day at the plant, especially if I know he's going to be on the floor. I'll be standing there, looking at a sample, and my shoulders will be practically up to my ears, I'm so tense. And then I come home, and the tension doesn't leave, it just turns into this bone-deep exhaustion. I sit on the couch, and I literally feel like I can't move my arms or legs, like I'm made of lead. 

But actual pain? Like a headache? No, not really. It's just... it's all in my chest and my mind, just this constant spinning and second-guessing. Like I was telling you about second-guessing those routine quality calls... it's like my brain is just working overtime, trying to anticipate every single thing he might criticize, and it just leaves my body feeling completely wrecked by the end of the week. But no, no stomach problems or headaches specifically. Just... everything else, it feels like.
Are you avoiding places or situations outside of work because of your thoughts and feelings about the new operations manager?

Well, no, not exactly avoiding places outside of work, not in the sense that I'm afraid to go out or anything like that. It's more just... I don't go anywhere because I don't have the energy, like I was saying before about feeling like I'm made of lead. It's not that I'm actively thinking, "Oh, I can't go to the grocery store because of the operations manager." It's more that by the time Saturday rolls around, I am so completely depleted from the week, from all that tension and second-guessing, that the very idea of leaving the house just feels like climbing a mountain. 

Mark and I used to go to this little diner on Sunday mornings, just a nice, quiet routine we had for years. We'd sit in our usual booth, drink coffee, maybe talk about the week ahead... but I haven't wanted to go in over a month. Not because I'm avoiding the diner, but because if I go, I know I'll just sit there staring into my coffee cup, completely zoned out, replaying whatever comment that manager made on Friday afternoon. I'd just be ruining Mark's breakfast, honestly. 

And my sister invited us over for a barbecue last weekend—which I usually love, I really do love seeing my nieces—but I just couldn't bring myself to go. I made up some excuse about feeling under the weather, which wasn't a total lie because I was exhausted, but the real reason was I just knew I wouldn't be able to hold a normal conversation. I knew my mind would be stuck back at the plant, agonizing over Monday's inspection schedule and wondering if he was going to implement those new reporting metrics he's been hinting at. I just didn't want to be a dark cloud at a family party, you know? So I just stayed home on the couch. 

But it's not like I'm afraid of running into him outside of work or anything. He lives two towns over, anyway. It's just that the stress he causes me at work is so heavy, it just squashes any desire I have to do anything else with my time off. I just want to sit in my quiet house and try to turn my brain off, even though, as I said before, I can't even seem to do that when I try to sleep. So, no, I'm not avoiding places, I'm just... I'm just avoiding life, I guess. Because I'm too tired to participate in it.
Do you think your fears or worries about the new operations manager are exaggerated or unreasonable?

Well, that's the thing, isn't it? I mean, I've spent hours... literally hours, lying awake at night, staring at the ceiling, asking myself that exact question. Am I just blowing this all out of proportion? Mark certainly seems to think so sometimes, when I'm pacing the living room on a Sunday night, practically in tears over a shift schedule. He'll say, "It's just a job, honey, he's just a manager," and I know he means well, I really do, but it just makes me feel like I'm crazy. 

But then I think about the reality of the situation at the plant. I mean, I've been doing quality control for fifteen years. Fifteen years! I know that line inside and out, I know what a good sample looks like, I know the tolerances... and I've never had a problem. My reviews have always been stellar. And now, this guy comes in from some corporate office, half my age, and he's completely upending everything. He's talking about "efficiency" and "streamlining," and every time he looks over my shoulder, I feel like he's just waiting for me to make a mistake so he can justify bringing in some automated system to replace me. 

So, are my fears exaggerated? I honestly don't know anymore. Sometimes I think, yes, maybe I'm overreacting, maybe he's just trying to make his mark and it's not a personal attack on me or my competence. Maybe I'm just resistant to change because I'm used to doing things a certain way. But then... then I remember the way he spoke to Sarah in shipping last week, just completely dismissed her concerns about the new packaging protocol in front of everyone. It was humiliating for her. And I think, what if he does that to me? What if I miss something because I'm so nervous, and he uses it as an excuse to write me up, or worse? 

At fifty-five, with an Associate's degree... where else am I going to go? Who else is going to hire me at my current salary? This job is my livelihood, it's our retirement plan, it's everything. So when I think about it like that, no, I don't think my fears are unreasonable at all. I think they're completely justified because the stakes are just so incredibly high for me. But then I circle back around to the fact that I'm missing deadlines and hiding from meetings, which is completely unlike me, and I wonder if the fear itself is what's going to get me fired, not the manager.
